newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan traders surprised by fall in CBOT soybeans.
newsitem.headline: Japan traders surprised by fall in CBOT soybeans.

text.p: Japanese traders said on Tuesday they were mildly surprised by the sharp fall in soybean and soymeal futures prices in Chicago and said they will continue to buy U.S. soybean for July shipment at a steady pace.
"We were a bit surprised by the price plunges in Chicago," a soybean trader at a major trade house in Tokyo said. "But it's not unusual to have such downward corrections after recent price rallies."
CBOT soybean futures crashed after the U.S. Department of Agriculture (USDA) said on Monday its 1996/97 soybean ending stocks were unchanged at 125 million bushels, dissapointing the market.
The CBOT soybean July contract fell 20-1/2 U.S. cents to end on Monday at US$8.68-1/2 a bushel.
Local traders are stepping up purchases of U.S. soybeans due to their uncertainty about the direction of U.S. soybean prices and the firmer tone of the U.S. Gulf/Japan freight rates.
A senior official of a major soybean crusher in Tokyo said: "There may be some temporary up and down on the Chicago market. But we're covering U.S. bean at constant pace."

All contracts on the Tokyo soybean futures market ended sharply lower on Tuesday, taking their cue from the drop in CBOT prices. The benchmark April 1998 contract was down 910 yen at 34,390 yen per tonne. The day's volume was 68,120 lots.
